Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
10 October 2026 .
· Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 The IRGC claims it struck a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz, per Asharq Al-Awsat English; the claim has not been independently confirmed.

02 CNBC reports tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have surged to a wartime high as Iran seeks to choke off oil exports; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 The Maritime Executive reports the IRGC has expanded its threat against non-compliant vessels as more tankers are struck.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic. The IRGC claims it struck a tanker transiting the waterway, per Asharq Al-Awsat English; no other outlet in this feed carries the claim independently. The Financial Times reports Iran has extended strikes on tankers beyond the strait into the broader Gulf, consistent with background reporting that attacks have spread across the region. CNBC reports attacks have surged to a wartime high as Iran seeks to choke off oil exports. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The oil price feed has not produced a print in over two hours; no price level is available. On the diplomatic front, background indicates Iran said it would answer Washington's reply to its seven-day plan within a few days, while President Trump has said the blockade stays in force and the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. Thirty-three headlines have been indexed in the last 24 hours. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flagged low-confidence because two of its inputs are stale or missing (the Brent-WTI forward spread and Manifold forward contracts), with Polymarket escalation contracts as its top contributor.
